pull.title: MINOR: Cherry-pick streams fixes and tests from trunk to 4.4
pull.body:
This collects cherry-picks from trunk to 4.4, opened to run CI on them together. The commits will be pushed to 4.4 individually rather than merged through this PR, so that each keeps its own commit and cherry-pick reference.

The fixes are KAFKA-20735, which avoids a spurious warning when a state manager without registered stores is closed, KAFKA-21212, which clears the rack ID when a static streams member rejoins without one, and KAFKA-21255, which returns the streams assignment whenever a member reports all its owned task sets. The other commits add test coverage for the topology description plugin (KIP-1331), cross-version system tests for the streams rebalance protocol and for static membership against older brokers, and a javadoc fix in CoordinatorResult. KAFKA-20817 is included because the KIP-1331 cross-version system tests build on its test file.

KAFKA-21255 needed small test changes on 4.4, described in its commit message: a change to a test of the assignment refiner is dropped, since the refiner is not on 4.4, and the new tests are adapted to the test utilities on this branch.

KAFKA-20735: Skip state-directory lock on close when there are no sto… (#22951)

With the state updater enabled, Streams could log a spurious WARN
(previously ERROR) — "Unable to acquire lock while closing the state
store for task " — during back-to-back rebalances, when a task's
per-task state-directory lock is transiently held by another thread as
the task is handed off. It's harmless (no data loss or lag) but pollutes
alerting.

StateManagerUtil.closeStateManager() now short-circuits when there is
nothing to close: if the state manager has no registered stores and
we're not wiping state, it returns early without acquiring the lock or
logging. When stores are still registered but the lock can't be
acquired, the WARN is still emitted, preserving signal for genuinely
unexpected failures. The unclean-EOS wipe path is unchanged.

Add package-private ProcessorStateManager.hasRegisteredStores().  Guard
the lock/close/log in closeStateManager() with !wipeStateStore &&
!stateMgr.hasRegisteredStores().  Update StateManagerUtilTest and add
shouldSkipLockAcquisitionWhenNoRegisteredStoresToClose.

 <lbrutschy@confluent.io>

KAFKA-20817: Add more ducktape system tests scenarios for topology description plugin (#23138)

## Summary
This PR adds 3 more system test scenarios for streams topology test.
1. `test_topology_description_not_resolicited_after_client_restart`:
client start with description already stored, the broker is already
running -> client restarted and since `storedDescriptionTopologyEpoch ==
currentTopologyEpoch`, the broker does not solicit again.
2. `test_topology_description_only_one_member_pushes`: two members join
the same streams group at the same time and both heartbeat to the broker
-> since `StreamsGroupTopologyDescriptionBackoff.armIfNotActive`'s
check-and-arm on the group's back-off entry is atomic, only one member's
heartbeat gets `TopologyDescriptionRequired=true`; the other member
never sends a push.
3.
`test_topology_description_resolicited_after_group_delete_and_recreate`:
client pushes successfully, then the group is stopped and deleted -> a
new client joins under the same application.id and since the delete
clears the old group's `storedDescriptionTopologyEpoch`, the broker
treats it as a brand-new group and solicits again.

<frankvicky@apache.org>

MINOR: Add cross-version compatibility tests for the KIP-1331 topology description plugin (#23413)

The heartbeat- and describe-based topology push protocol added by
KIP-1331 relies on StreamsGroupHeartbeat and StreamsGroupDescribe
negotiating down to earlier versions when talking to a broker or client
that predates the feature, and on the admin client refusing to send a
topology description request a broker cannot understand. This was
previously only checked by unit tests exercising the version-gating
logic directly; nothing ran an actual pre-4.4 Kafka broker or Streams
client against the feature to prove the real wire negotiation degrades
gracefully in both directions.

This adds three system tests covering the missing directions: a Streams
client built from this branch (topology push enabled by default) talking
to a genuine 4.3.1 broker, a genuine 4.3.1 Streams client talking to a
broker on this branch with the plugin configured, and the admin
client/CLI on this branch requesting a topology description from a 4.3.1
broker, which must fail client-side with UnsupportedVersionException
rather than silently describing the group without it.

## Test plan

All three tests were run against real ducker containers (docker-based
ducktape harness) to confirm they exercise the intended code paths
rather than passing vacuously:
- Confirmed via broker/client logs that the pinned old-version processes
actually ran Kafka 4.3.1, not the dev-branch build.
- Confirmed the admin-client test's failure text matches
`UnsupportedVersionException: Attempted to write a non-default
includeTopologyDescription at version 0` with exit code 1.
- Re-ran the full `streams_topology_description_plugin_test.py` suite (9
tests) plus the new smoke test together; all pass.

Reviewers: TengYao Chi <frankvicky@apache.org>
(cherry picked from commit fb48d18e5fded3cf15b1efc4d7283a1d3b776bc2)

KAFKA-20697: Add cross-version system tests for the streams rebalance protocol (#23146)

Kafka 4.4 bumps `StreamsGroupHeartbeat` and `StreamsGroupDescribe` from
v0 to v1 (KIP-1331, KIP-1357, KAFKA-20744). The new fields only flow
when both sides are 4.4+, so this adds ducktape coverage for
mixed-version deployments in both directions, using 4.2.1/4.3.1 as the
older side (4.2 is the earliest release with streams group support). The
tests drive the `StreamsUpgradeTest` harness with
`group.protocol=streams`.

New `streams_protocol_cross_version_test.py` (7 tests, 15 matrix cases):
- new client / old broker: reaches RUNNING, logs
`acceptableRecoveryLag=not provided (older broker)` exactly when the
response was v0, no `UnsupportedVersionException`
- old client / new broker: reaches RUNNING, the ignorable v1 lag field
is dropped cleanly at v0
- `MISSING_CLIENT_TAGS` is only sent to v1 clients, and not sent when
the required tag is configured
- `kafka-streams-groups.sh --describe` works cross-version in both
directions; `--describe --topology` against an old broker fails
diagnosably rather than hanging (graceful degradation is a possible
follow-up; the assertion is deliberately loose so it survives one)
- a plugin-configured new broker reports no stored topology description
for an old client

Extended `streams_topology_description_plugin_test.py` (+1 test): a new
client is never solicited for a topology push by an old broker, since
`TopologyDescriptionRequired` only exists in response v1. `setup_kafka`
gained an optional `broker_version` parameter; existing tests unchanged.

The warm-up scenario from the ticket (old clients must never get warm-up
tasks) is intentionally left out: `AssignmentRefiner` is still a stub,
so the test would pass vacuously until KAFKA-20665 lands.

Reviewers: Matthias J. Sax <matthias@confluent.io>, Lucas Brutschy
<lbrutschy@confluent.io>

(cherry picked from commit 9987c5ba125cd31bf321333c9a19cea549807f99)

KAFKA-20971: Add system test for streams static membership against old broker (#23523)

Adds a system test verifying that a newer (dev/4.4+) Kafka Streams
client using static membership on the `streams` group protocol correctly
detects and fails against an older broker (4.2/4.3) that doesn't support
the `streams` group protocol.

The client sends a `STREAMS_GROUP_HEARTBEAT` request, which the old
broker rejects with `INVALID_REQUEST` ("Static membership is not yet
supported"). The client then transitions to the terminal `ERROR` state
rather than hanging or retrying indefinitely.

Note on scope: this PR originally also covered the reverse case (old
client vs new broker), but that direction fails with a client-side
`ConfigException` during `StreamsConfig` construction, before any broker
contact. This is a local configuration guard rather than a cross-version
compatibility issue, and is already covered by unit tests. Per
discussion on the ticket, that direction has been dropped from this PR.

Testing:

* Verified against Kafka 4.2.1.
* Verified against Kafka 4.3.1.
* Ran the test both in isolation and as part of the full
`StreamsStaticMembershipTest` suite.

Reviewers: Lucas Brutschy <lbrutschy@confluent.io>
(cherry picked from commit 81d676c8b4a0f60ed69511fa1a74a2c9e3f44489)

MINOR: Fix CoordinatorResult javadoc and strengthen streams delay-timer tests (#23619)

The replayRecords javadoc described it as "the records to replay", even
though it is a boolean flag controlling whether the coordinator applies
records to its in-memory state, not a list of records.

The two streams initial-rebalance-delay tests also could not tell
whether the target assignment they observed came from the delay timer
actually replaying its records, or from a later heartbeat recomputing
the assignment on its own, since both tests only checked the group state
after an additional heartbeat had already run past the timer firing.
They now assert the in-memory target assignment right after the timer
fires and before any further heartbeat, and the first test performs an
extra heartbeat inside the delay window so the topology is configured on
the persisted group rather than a throwaway instance, which is required
for the timer to compute and replay the assignment in the first place.

Reviewers: Sean Quah <squah@confluent.io>
(cherry picked from commit 3c7b0661c132fc07b6e8da9daf991e31b0363b3e)

commit.message:
MINOR: Prove topology.description.push.enabled=false suppresses the update RPC end-to-end (#23658)

This adds an integration test alongside
`TopologyDescriptionPluginIntegrationTest` that runs a Streams app with
`topology.description.push.enabled=false` against a broker configured
with the tracking topology description plugin used in that test class.
Today the client-side suppression is only unit-tested at

`StreamThreadTest.shouldNotPopulateWireTopologyDescriptionWhenPushDisabled`,
which only checks that the client does not populate the wire topology
description object; it does not prove the behavior end-to-end against a
real broker.

The new test keeps the group alive without a stored topology
description, so the broker keeps soliciting the push on every heartbeat
exactly as it does for a push-enabled client (same mechanism already
exercised by `shouldPushTopologyDescriptionToPluginAfterJoin` in the
same class). Waiting across several heartbeat intervals and asserting
the plugin's `setTopology` is never invoked and the group's topology
description status stays `NOT_STORED` shows that the suppression is a
genuine client-side opt-out rather than something that happens to work
because the broker never asks.

### Test plan
- `./gradlew :streams:integration-tests:test --tests

"org.apache.kafka.streams.integration.TopologyDescriptionPluginIntegrationTest"`
passes, including the new
`shouldNotPushTopologyDescriptionWhenDisabledByClient` test.

Reviewers: Bill Bejeck <bbejeck@apache.org>
(cherry picked from commit ed44e4baf8b8571ca6a6298f1bfe2409ae2b4a4a)

MINOR: Add broker integration tests for classic JoinGroup topology cleanup (#23747)

Converting an empty streams group to a classic group requires the broker
to delete the group's stored topology description from the plugin first.
This path was only unit-tested against mocks; no test sent a real
classic JoinGroupRequest to a running broker, and the failed-join and
periodic-cleanup halves were never chained together.

This adds three single-broker integration tests to
StreamsGroupTopologyDescriptionRequestTest. The first joins a classic
member to an empty streams group with a stored topology and checks that
the broker calls plugin.deleteTopology and converts the group. The
second makes deleteTopology fail and checks that the join is rejected
with the retriable REBALANCE_IN_PROGRESS while the group stays a streams
group. The third chains the failure with the periodic cleanup cycle:
after the plugin recovers, the cycle clears the stored topology without
any client involvement, and a later classic join converts the group.

FailingTopologyDescriptionPlugin gains a per-group counter of
deleteTopology invocations, so the tests can assert that the broker
actually reached the plugin.

(cherry picked from commit 3c1b3f2db34b2191c00bd97d3de92c4945668ab6)

commit.message:
KAFKA-21212: Fix rack ID removal on Streams static member rejoin. (#23705)

Fixes KAFKA-21212

When a Streams static member restarted after removing `client.rack`, the
coordinator retained the previous rack ID. During static member
replacement, the coordinator copies the previous member’s metadata, then
applies the incoming updates. Because `maybeUpdateRackId` treats null as
unchanged, the joining request could not clear the copied rack ID. This
left stale rack information in group descriptions and custom assignor
inputs.

This change distinguishes joining requests from regular heartbeats,
following the existing handling of `userEndpoint`. Joining requests now
apply the rack ID directly, including null to clear the previous value.
Regular heartbeats continue to preserve the existing rack ID when the
field is omitted. Clearing a previously configured rack ID also allows
the existing metadata change detection to bump the group epoch and
trigger assignment recomputation.

Reviewers: Lucas Brutschy <lbrutschy@confluent.io>
(cherry picked from commit 0661cd0bb4531c742586c2955183822b54c838ce)

commit.message:
KAFKA-21255: Return Streams assignments when all owned task sets are reported. (#23768)

Fixes KAFKA-21255.

Return the current assignment in StreamsGroupHeartbeat responses
whenever the request includes all three owned task sets(active, standby,
and warmup) including empty sets. This allows clients to recover a
missed assignment after heartbeat response loss, even when processing
the retry does not change the coordinator’s assignment.

Reviewers: Lucas Brutschy <lbrutschy@confluent.io>
(cherry picked from commit 5f684cca20c4a9c096bfa7497a254eed50bc7d5d)

Backport note: dropped the change to a test of the assignment refiner, which is not on 4.4. In the new tests, added the missing StreamsGroupTestUtil imports and used getDefaultAssignmentConfigs(), since 4.4 stores the last assignment configs as a map.

KAFKA-20735: Skip state-directory lock on close when there are no sto… (#22951)

With the state updater enabled, Streams could log a spurious WARN
(previously ERROR) — "Unable to acquire lock while closing the state
store for task " — during back-to-back rebalances, when a task's
per-task state-directory lock is transiently held by another thread as
the task is handed off. It's harmless (no data loss or lag) but pollutes
alerting.

StateManagerUtil.closeStateManager() now short-circuits when there is
nothing to close: if the state manager has no registered stores and
we're not wiping state, it returns early without acquiring the lock or
logging. When stores are still registered but the lock can't be
acquired, the WARN is still emitted, preserving signal for genuinely
unexpected failures. The unclean-EOS wipe path is unchanged.

Add package-private ProcessorStateManager.hasRegisteredStores().  Guard
the lock/close/log in closeStateManager() with !wipeStateStore &&
!stateMgr.hasRegisteredStores().  Update StateManagerUtilTest and add
shouldSkipLockAcquisitionWhenNoRegisteredStoresToClose.

MINOR: Add cross-version compatibility tests for the KIP-1331 topology description plugin (#23413)

The heartbeat- and describe-based topology push protocol added by
KIP-1331 relies on StreamsGroupHeartbeat and StreamsGroupDescribe
negotiating down to earlier versions when talking to a broker or client
that predates the feature, and on the admin client refusing to send a
topology description request a broker cannot understand. This was
previously only checked by unit tests exercising the version-gating
logic directly; nothing ran an actual pre-4.4 Kafka broker or Streams
client against the feature to prove the real wire negotiation degrades
gracefully in both directions.

This adds three system tests covering the missing directions: a Streams
client built from this branch (topology push enabled by default) talking
to a genuine 4.3.1 broker, a genuine 4.3.1 Streams client talking to a
broker on this branch with the plugin configured, and the admin
client/CLI on this branch requesting a topology description from a 4.3.1
broker, which must fail client-side with UnsupportedVersionException
rather than silently describing the group without it.

## Test plan

All three tests were run against real ducker containers (docker-based
ducktape harness) to confirm they exercise the intended code paths
rather than passing vacuously:
- Confirmed via broker/client logs that the pinned old-version processes
actually ran Kafka 4.3.1, not the dev-branch build.
- Confirmed the admin-client test's failure text matches
`UnsupportedVersionException: Attempted to write a non-default
includeTopologyDescription at version 0` with exit code 1.
- Re-ran the full `streams_topology_description_plugin_test.py` suite (9
tests) plus the new smoke test together; all pass.

(cherry picked from commit fb48d18e5fded3cf15b1efc4d7283a1d3b776bc2)

KAFKA-20697: Add cross-version system tests for the streams rebalance protocol (#23146)

Kafka 4.4 bumps `StreamsGroupHeartbeat` and `StreamsGroupDescribe` from
v0 to v1 (KIP-1331, KIP-1357, KAFKA-20744). The new fields only flow
when both sides are 4.4+, so this adds ducktape coverage for
mixed-version deployments in both directions, using 4.2.1/4.3.1 as the
older side (4.2 is the earliest release with streams group support). The
tests drive the `StreamsUpgradeTest` harness with
`group.protocol=streams`.

New `streams_protocol_cross_version_test.py` (7 tests, 15 matrix cases):
- new client / old broker: reaches RUNNING, logs
`acceptableRecoveryLag=not provided (older broker)` exactly when the
response was v0, no `UnsupportedVersionException`
- old client / new broker: reaches RUNNING, the ignorable v1 lag field
is dropped cleanly at v0

KAFKA-20971: Add system test for streams static membership against old broker (#23523)

Adds a system test verifying that a newer (dev/4.4+) Kafka Streams
client using static membership on the `streams` group protocol correctly
detects and fails against an older broker (4.2/4.3) that doesn't support
the `streams` group protocol.

The client sends a `STREAMS_GROUP_HEARTBEAT` request, which the old
broker rejects with `INVALID_REQUEST` ("Static membership is not yet
supported"). The client then transitions to the terminal `ERROR` state
rather than hanging or retrying indefinitely.

Note on scope: this PR originally also covered the reverse case (old
client vs new broker), but that direction fails with a client-side
`ConfigException` during `StreamsConfig` construction, before any broker
contact. This is a local configuration guard rather than a cross-version
compatibility issue, and is already covered by unit tests. Per
discussion on the ticket, that direction has been dropped from this PR.

Testing:

* Verified against Kafka 4.2.1.
* Verified against Kafka 4.3.1.
* Ran the test both in isolation and as part of the full
`StreamsStaticMembershipTest` suite.

MINOR: Fix CoordinatorResult javadoc and strengthen streams delay-timer tests (#23619)

The replayRecords javadoc described it as "the records to replay", even
though it is a boolean flag controlling whether the coordinator applies
records to its in-memory state, not a list of records.

The two streams initial-rebalance-delay tests also could not tell
whether the target assignment they observed came from the delay timer
actually replaying its records, or from a later heartbeat recomputing
the assignment on its own, since both tests only checked the group state
after an additional heartbeat had already run past the timer firing.
They now assert the in-memory target assignment right after the timer
fires and before any further heartbeat, and the first test performs an
extra heartbeat inside the delay window so the topology is configured on
the persisted group rather than a throwaway instance, which is required

MINOR: Prove topology.description.push.enabled=false suppresses the update RPC end-to-end (#23658)

This adds an integration test alongside
`TopologyDescriptionPluginIntegrationTest` that runs a Streams app with
`topology.description.push.enabled=false` against a broker configured
with the tracking topology description plugin used in that test class.
Today the client-side suppression is only unit-tested at

`StreamThreadTest.shouldNotPopulateWireTopologyDescriptionWhenPushDisabled`,
which only checks that the client does not populate the wire topology
description object; it does not prove the behavior end-to-end against a
real broker.

The new test keeps the group alive without a stored topology
description, so the broker keeps soliciting the push on every heartbeat
exactly as it does for a push-enabled client (same mechanism already
exercised by `shouldPushTopologyDescriptionToPluginAfterJoin` in the
same class). Waiting across several heartbeat intervals and asserting
the plugin's `setTopology` is never invoked and the group's topology
description status stays `NOT_STORED` shows that the suppression is a
genuine client-side opt-out rather than something that happens to work
because the broker never asks.

### Test plan
- `./gradlew :streams:integration-tests:test --tests

"org.apache.kafka.streams.integration.TopologyDescriptionPluginIntegrationTest"`
passes, including the new
`shouldNotPushTopologyDescriptionWhenDisabledByClient` test.

MINOR: Add broker integration tests for topology-description plugin failure surfacing (#23670)

StreamsGroupTopologyDescriptionRequestTest only ever exercises
InMemoryTopologyDescriptionPlugin, which never fails, so the permanent
and transient failure classification for the
StreamsGroupTopologyDescriptionUpdate RPC, and the DeleteGroups
plugin-failure path, were proven only against mocks in
GroupCoordinatorServiceTopologyDescriptionTest, never against a real
broker/RPC round trip.

This adds FailingTopologyDescriptionPlugin, a configurable test double
whose setTopology and deleteTopology calls can be told to fail on
demand, and three new cluster tests built on it. A permanent setTopology
failure surfaces STREAMS_TOPOLOGY_DESCRIPTION_UPDATE_FAILED with the
plugin's message and stops the broker from re-soliciting a push at that
epoch. A transient failure returns the same error code but arms the
heartbeat back-off instead of ratcheting the epoch. A DeleteGroups
plugin failure returns GROUP_DELETION_FAILED without tombstoning the
group, and a retried delete succeeds once the plugin recovers.

timeline.message:
MINOR: Add broker integration tests for classic JoinGroup topology cleanup (#23747)

Converting an empty streams group to a classic group requires the broker
to delete the group's stored topology description from the plugin first.
This path was only unit-tested against mocks; no test sent a real
classic JoinGroupRequest to a running broker, and the failed-join and
periodic-cleanup halves were never chained together.

This adds three single-broker integration tests to
StreamsGroupTopologyDescriptionRequestTest. The first joins a classic
member to an empty streams group with a stored topology and checks that
the broker calls plugin.deleteTopology and converts the group. The
second makes deleteTopology fail and checks that the join is rejected
with the retriable REBALANCE_IN_PROGRESS while the group stays a streams
group. The third chains the failure with the periodic cleanup cycle:
after the plugin recovers, the cycle clears the stored topology without
any client involvement, and a later classic join converts the group.

FailingTopologyDescriptionPlugin gains a per-group counter of
deleteTopology invocations, so the tests can assert that the broker
actually reached the plugin.

Reviewers: TengYao Chi <frankvicky@apache.org>
(cherry picked from commit 3c1b3f2db34b2191c00bd97d3de92c4945668ab6)

timeline.message:
KAFKA-21212: Fix rack ID removal on Streams static member rejoin. (#23705)

Fixes KAFKA-21212

When a Streams static member restarted after removing `client.rack`, the
coordinator retained the previous rack ID. During static member
replacement, the coordinator copies the previous member’s metadata, then
applies the incoming updates. Because `maybeUpdateRackId` treats null as
unchanged, the joining request could not clear the copied rack ID. This
left stale rack information in group descriptions and custom assignor
inputs.

This change distinguishes joining requests from regular heartbeats,
following the existing handling of `userEndpoint`. Joining requests now
apply the rack ID directly, including null to clear the previous value.
Regular heartbeats continue to preserve the existing rack ID when the
field is omitted. Clearing a previously configured rack ID also allows
the existing metadata change detection to bump the group epoch and
trigger assignment recomputation.

Reviewers: Lucas Brutschy <lbrutschy@confluent.io>
(cherry picked from commit 0661cd0bb4531c742586c2955183822b54c838ce)

Fixes KAFKA-21255.

Return the current assignment in StreamsGroupHeartbeat responses
whenever the request includes all three owned task sets(active, standby,
and warmup) including empty sets. This allows clients to recover a
missed assignment after heartbeat response loss, even when processing
the retry does not change the coordinator’s assignment.
